grammar.label: parallel structure in lists and comparisons
grammar.meaning: items joined by and, or or than take the same grammatical shape

explanation.en: 'The course improves reading, writing and listening' matches three nouns. 'The course improves reading, writing and to listen' breaks the pattern and reads as an error. Comparisons must match too: 'writing a report is harder than writing a letter', not 'than a letter'.
explanation.uz: 'and', 'or', 'than' bilan bog'langan bo'laklar bir xil grammatik shaklda bo'lishi kerak. Shakl buzilsa, gap xato eshitiladi.

grammar.positive_example: The post requires accuracy, patience and a good ear.
grammar.negative_example: The post requires accuracy, patience and to have a good ear.

l1_notes.uz: Parallel tuzilma ingliz yozma uslubining asosiy talabi; ro'yxatlarda har bir band bir xil shaklda boshlanadi.

grammar.label: correlative pairs — not only … but also, either … or, neither … nor
grammar.meaning: binds two elements into one balanced statement

explanation.en: The two halves must frame the same kind of element: 'not only the cost but also the delay' (two nouns) is right; 'not only the cost but also it was late' is not. With 'neither … nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
explanation.uz: Ikki qism bir xil turdagi bo'lakni qamrab olishi kerak. 'neither … nor' da fe'l yaqinroq egaga moslashadi.

grammar.positive_example: Not only the cost but also the delay worried the committee.
grammar.negative_example: Not only the cost but also it was delayed worried the committee.

l1_notes.uz: Juft bog'lovchining ikkala qismi ham albatta ishlatiladi; birini tashlab ketish xato.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The programme is not only for the children but also their parents can come.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The two halves do not match. One is a phrase and one is a sentence.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: 'Not only for the children but also for their parents.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Now they match. Whatever follows 'not only' must follow 'but also'.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The next line lists what the evening is: 'reading, a film and to talk about the school'.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Two of them are nouns and the third is not.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: 'Reading, a film and a discussion of the school.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Three nouns, and the line stops pulling against itself.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Bobur wrote the part about the music.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'Either the ensemble will play, or a soloist.' That one is fine.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Neither he nor I could say why it is fine.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Because the shape on the left is the shape on the right. That is all parallel means.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then I will read every list twice from now on, once for sense and once for shape.
